title: World Cup Day 2: USA beat Paraguay 4-1; Canada and Bosnia & Herzegovina drew 1-1
excerpt: Group stage action from Toronto, Los Angeles on June 12 — 2 matches, no shortage of drama.
body:
Day 2 of the 2026 FIFA World Cup delivered 2 matches and 7 goals on Friday, June 12. The tournament, spread across the United States, Canada, and Mexico, continued its group stage with action that will resonate in standings tables and living rooms alike — not least in the Indian-American households tuning in from cities that are, for once, hosting the spectacle rather than streaming it from half a world away.

Here is everything you need to know.

Canada 1-1 Bosnia & Herzegovina

Group B · BMO Field, Toronto

A 1-1 draw was probably a fair reflection of a tightly contested match between Canada and Bosnia & Herzegovina at BMO Field. Both teams created chances, both teams scored, and both teams will look at moments where they might have won it. In the end, a share of the spoils was the just outcome.

For both sides, the arithmetic is clear: a point is better than none, but wins are the currency of a group stage. Their remaining Group B fixtures take on added importance.

USA 4-1 Paraguay

Group D · SoFi Stadium, Los Angeles

"In the end, a share of the spoils was the just outcome."

USA made a resounding statement in Group D, dismantling Paraguay 4-1 at SoFi Stadium. From the opening whistle, they looked a level above, converting chance after chance with clinical efficiency. Paraguay will need to regroup quickly; in a group stage this compressed, a heavy defeat on goal difference can haunt a team in the final reckoning.

The 4-goal haul will send a message to the rest of Group D, and perhaps beyond it. USA's depth was evident throughout — substitutes looked just as sharp as starters, a promising sign for the knockout rounds.

!World Cup — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

The match took place at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles, where the growing South Asian community turned out in force. For many Indian-American fans in LA, this was a once-in-a-lifetime chance to see World Cup football without a transatlantic flight.

What It Means for the Standings

In Group B, Canada and Bosnia & Herzegovina each take a point — not the worst outcome, but not the result either side wanted. In Group D, USA move to 3 points and put themselves in a strong position; Paraguay sit on zero points and will need results in their remaining fixtures.

With 48 teams and a format that sends the top two from each group — plus the eight best third-placed sides — into the round of 32, the margins are tighter than they appear. Goal difference could prove decisive.

What's Next

Day 3 (Saturday, June 13) brings 3 more group stage matches:

  • Qatar vs Switzerland — Group B at Levi's Stadium, San Francisco Bay Area
  • Brazil vs Morocco — Group C at MetLife Stadium, New York/New Jersey
  • Haiti vs Scotland — Group C at Gillette Stadium, Boston
